#Data Pre-processing:

In this step, we want to:

1. Read the data
```{r}
ev_data <- read.csv("Data/EV_Charging/EV_Charging_Data-_Municipal_Lots_and_Garages_20251106.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
```

2. Choose ID tag as an unique identifier:
```{r}

# Choose ID_tag as unique identifier
# Check if ID_tag is unique
sum(duplicated(ev_data$`ID Tag`))
# Keep only the first row per ID_tag
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  distinct(`ID Tag`, .keep_all = TRUE)

```

3. Remove Columns and rows that are not relevent to our experiment:
```{r}
# Remove columns: Driver_id, Invalidity_reason, country
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  select(-`Driver ID`, -`Invalidity Reason`, -`Country`)

# Remove rows where session_status is “Disconnected”
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  filter(`Session Status` != "DISCONNECTED")

# Keep Station_name and drop Charger_id
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  select(-`Charge Box ID`)

# Check null values and drop rows with any NA
colSums(is.na(ev_data))
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  tidyr::drop_na()
```

4.Convert type from chr to numeric
```{r}
#change Charge Duration (min) to numeric
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(`Charge Duration (min)` = as.numeric(gsub(",", "", `Charge Duration (min)`)))
#change Connected Duration (min) to numeric
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(`Connected Duration (min)` = as.numeric(gsub(",", "", `Connected Duration (min)`)))
```

5. Add columns based on Dates
```{r}

# Sort the data based on date
ev_data$Date <- as.Date(ev_data$Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Add weekday column
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(weekday = weekdays(Date))

# Add is_weekend
weekends <- c("Saturday", "Sunday")
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    is_weekend = weekday %in% weekends
  )

# Add holidays column for year 2024
# Need to work on this!!
holidays_2024 <- as.Date(c(
  "2024-01-01", # New Year's Day
  "2024-01-15", # MLK Day
  "2024-02-19", # Presidents' Day
  "2024-05-27", # Memorial Day
  "2024-06-19", # Juneteenth
  "2024-07-04", # Independence Day
  "2024-09-02", # Labor Day
  "2024-10-14", # Columbus/Indigenous Peoples' Day
  "2024-11-11", # Veterans Day
  "2024-11-28", # Thanksgiving
  "2024-12-25"  # Christmas
))

ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    is_holiday_2024 = Date %in% holidays_2024
  )


```


6. Clean the location names:

```{r}

# Standardize location names
ev_data <- ev_data %>%
  mutate(
    `Location Name` = case_when(
      # Jerome Gun Hill Road variations
      grepl("JGU|Jerome.*Gun Hill", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Jerome Gun Hill Road Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Bay Ridge variations
      grepl("BRI|Bay Ridge", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Bay Ridge Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Delancey and Essex variations
      grepl("DES|Delancey.*Essex", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Delancey and Essex Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Queens Borough Hall variations
      grepl("QBO|Queensboro Hall|Queens Borough Hall", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Queens Borough Hall Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Jerome 190th Street variations
      grepl("JON|Jerome.*190", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Jerome 190th Street Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # St. George Courthouse variations
      grepl("SGE|St\\.? George", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "St. George Courthouse Garage",
      
      # Court Square variations
      grepl("CSQ|Court Square", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Court Square Municipal Parking Garage",
      
      # Queens Family Court variations
      grepl("QFA|Queens Family Court", `Location Name`, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 
        "Queens Family Court Municipal Garage",
      
      # Handle N/A
      `Location Name` == "N/A" ~ NA_character_,
      
      # Keep everything else as is
      TRUE ~ `Location Name`
    )
  )

# Check the results
unique(ev_data$`Location Name`)

# Count how many of each location
ev_data %>% count(`Location Name`, sort = TRUE)

```

7. Data info:

```{r}

head(ev_data, 10)

cat("Column names:\n")

write.csv(ev_data, "EV_data_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Descriptive Analysis

### Frequency Tables

1. Frequency table → Session Status distribution; Weekday distribution; Location distribution

```{r}
# 1. Session Status distribution
session_status_freq <- ev_data %>%
  count(`Session Status`, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = n / sum(n) * 100,
    percentage = round(percentage, 2)
  )

# Session Status bar chart
ggplot(session_status_freq, aes(x = reorder(`Session Status`, -n), y = n)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Session Status Distribution", x = "Status", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

print(session_status_freq)

# 2. Weekday distribution
weekday_freq <- ev_data %>%
  count(weekday, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = n / sum(n) * 100,
    percentage = round(percentage, 2)
  )

# Weekday bar chart
ggplot(weekday_freq, aes(x = reorder(weekday, -n), y = n)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Weekday Distribution", x = "Day", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

print(weekday_freq)

# 3. Location distribution
location_freq <- ev_data %>%
  count(`Location Name`, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = n / sum(n) * 100,
    percentage = round(percentage, 2)
  )

# Location bar chart
ggplot(location_freq, aes(x = reorder(`Location Name`, -n), y = n)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "coral") +
  coord_flip() +  # Flip for better readability
  labs(title = "Location Distribution", x = "Location", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

print(location_freq)

```


## Absolute Frequency Tables

```{r absolute-frequency-tables}
# For categorical variables
categorical_vars <- sapply(data, is.factor)
cat_data <- data[, categorical_vars, drop = FALSE]

if(ncol(cat_data) > 0) {
  for(var in names(cat_data)) {
    cat("\n### Absolute Frequency Table for", var, "\n")
    freq_table <- table(cat_data[[var]])
    print(kable(freq_table, col.names = c(var, "Frequency"), 
                caption = paste("Absolute Frequency Table for", var)) %>%
          kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")))
  }
} else {
  cat("No categorical variables found in the dataset.\n")
}

# For numerical variables (binned)
numerical_vars <- sapply(data, is.numeric)
num_data <- data[, numerical_vars, drop = FALSE]

for(var in names(num_data)[1:2]) {  # Show first 2 numerical variables as example
  cat("\n### Binned Frequency Table for", var, "\n")
  breaks <- pretty(num_data[[var]], n = 8)
  freq_table <- table(cut(num_data[[var]], breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))
  print(kable(freq_table, col.names = c("Interval", "Frequency"),
              caption = paste("Binned Frequency Table for", var)) %>%
        kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")))
}
```

## Relative Frequency Tables

```{r relative-frequency-tables}
# For categorical variables
if(ncol(cat_data) > 0) {
```

# Summary Statistics

## Measures of Center and Dispersion

```{r summary-statistics}
# Function to calculate comprehensive summary statistics
comprehensive_summary <- function(x) {
  if(is.numeric(x)) {
    stats <- c(
      Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Mode = as.numeric(names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1]),
      "Trimmed Mean (10%)" = mean(x, trim = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
      "Trimmed Mean (20%)" = mean(x, trim = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE),
      IQR = IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Variance = var(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      "Std Deviation" = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      "Coeff of Variation" = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      Skewness = skewness(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Kurtosis = kurtosis(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Min = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Range = diff(range(x, na.rm = TRUE))
    )
    return(round(stats, 4))
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
}

# Apply to all numerical variables
summary_stats <- sapply(num_data, comprehensive_summary)
summary_stats <- as.data.frame(summary_stats)

kable(summary_stats, 
      caption = "Comprehensive Summary Statistics for Numerical Variables") %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"))
```

# Histograms

```{r histograms, fig.height=9}
if(ncol(num_data) > 0) {
  plots_list <- list()
  
  for(i in seq_along(names(num_data))) {
    var <- names(num_data)[i]
    var_data <- num_data[[var]]
    
    # Calculate statistics
    mean_val <- mean(var_data, na.rm = TRUE)
    median_val <- median(var_data, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Determine optimal number of bins using Freedman-Diaconis rule
    iqr_val <- IQR(var_data, na.rm = TRUE)
    n <- length(var_data[!is.na(var_data)])
    bin_width <- 2 * iqr_val / (n^(1/3))
    n_bins <- ceiling(diff(range(var_data, na.rm = TRUE)) / bin_width)
    n_bins <- max(5, min(n_bins, 30))  # Ensure reasonable number of bins
    
    p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = var)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = n_bins, fill = "lightblue", 
                     alpha = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = mean_val, color = "red", 
                 linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = median_val, color = "blue", 
                 linetype = "solid", linewidth = 1) +
      labs(title = paste("Histogram of", var, "(", n_bins, "bins)"),
           subtitle = paste("Red line: Mean (", round(mean_val, 2), 
                          "), Blue line: Median (", round(median_val, 2), ")"),
           x = var, y = "Frequency") +
      theme_minimal()
    
    plots_list[[i]] <- p
  }
  
  # Arrange plots
  do.call(grid.arrange, c(plots_list, ncol = 2))
}
```

# Box-Cox Transformations

```{r normality-tests}
# Test for normality before Box-Cox transformation
normality_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  Shapiro_p_value = numeric(),
  Normal = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

if(ncol(num_data) > 0) {
  for(var in names(num_data)) {
    var_data <- num_data[[var]]
    var_data <- var_data[!is.na(var_data) & var_data > 0]  # Box-Cox requires positive values
    
    if(length(var_data) > 3 && length(var_data) <= 5000) {  # Shapiro-Wilk limitations
      shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(var_data)
      is_normal <- shapiro_test$p.value > 0.05
      
      normality_results <- rbind(normality_results, data.frame(
        Variable = var,
        Shapiro_p_value = round(shapiro_test$p.value, 6),
        Normal = ifelse(is_normal, "Yes (p > 0.05)", "No (p ≤ 0.05)")
      ))
    }
  }
  
  kable(normality_results, 
        caption = "Normality Test Results (Shapiro-Wilk Test)") %>%
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"))
}
```

```{r box-cox-transformations, fig.height=11}
# Apply Box-Cox transformation to non-normal variables
if(ncol(num_data) > 0) {
  non_normal_vars <- normality_results$Variable[normality_results$Normal == "No (p ≤ 0.05)"]
  
  if(length(non_normal_vars) > 0) {
    cat("Applying Box-Cox transformations to non-normal variables:\n")
    
    plots_list <- list()
    transformation_summary <- data.frame(
      Variable = character(),
      Lambda = numeric(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    for(var in non_normal_vars) {
      var_data <- num_data[[var]]
      var_data <- var_data[!is.na(var_data) & var_data > 0]
      
      if(length(var_data) > 0 && all(var_data > 0)) {
        # Find optimal lambda
        bc_result <- boxCox(lm(var_data ~ 1), plotit = FALSE)
        lambda <- bc_result$x[which.max(bc_result$y)]
        
        # Apply Box-Cox transformation
        if(abs(lambda) < 1e-6) {
          transformed_data <- log(var_data)
          transform_label <- "Log transformation (λ ≈ 0)"
        } else {
          transformed_data <- (var_data^lambda - 1) / lambda
          transform_label <- paste("Box-Cox transformation (λ =", round(lambda, 3), ")")
        }
        
        # Store transformation info
        transformation_summary <- rbind(transformation_summary, data.frame(
          Variable = var,
          Lambda = round(lambda, 4)
        ))
        
        # Create before/after plots
        p1 <- ggplot(data.frame(x = var_data), aes(x = x)) +
          geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "lightcoral", alpha = 0.7) +
          labs(title = paste("Before:", var), x = var, y = "Frequency") +
          theme_minimal()
        
        p2 <- ggplot(data.frame(x = transformed_data), aes(x = x)) +
          geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "lightgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
          labs(title = paste("After:", transform_label), 
               x = paste("Transformed", var), y = "Frequency") +
          theme_minimal()
        
        # Q-Q plots
        p3 <- ggplot(data.frame(x = var_data), aes(sample = x)) +
          stat_qq() + stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
          labs(title = paste("Q-Q Before:", var)) +
          theme_minimal()
        
        p4 <- ggplot(data.frame(x = transformed_data), aes(sample = x)) +
          stat_qq() + stat_qq_line(color = "red") +
          labs(title = paste("Q-Q After:", transform_label)) +
          theme_minimal()
        
        # Combine plots
        combined_plot <- grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2,
                                    top = paste("Box-Cox Transformation for", var))
        plots_list[[length(plots_list) + 1]] <- combined_plot
      }
    }
    
    # Display transformation summary
    if(nrow(transformation_summary) > 0) {
      kable(transformation_summary, 
            caption = "Box-Cox Transformation Parameters") %>%
        kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"))
    }
    
  } else {
    cat("All variables appear to be normally distributed. No Box-Cox transformation needed.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No numerical variables available for Box-Cox transformation.\n")
}
```

```{r final-summary}
cat("Total variables:", ncol(data), "\n")
cat("Numerical variables:", sum(sapply(data, is.numeric)), "\n")
cat("Categorical variables:", sum(sapply(data, is.factor)), "\n")

if(exists("normality_results") && nrow(normality_results) > 0) {
  normal_count <- sum(grepl("Yes", normality_results$Normal))
  cat("Variables following normal distribution:", normal_count, "out of", nrow(normality_results), "\n")
}
```
